newsitem.title: CHINA: China steel firm awaits HK listing despite woes.
newsitem.headline: China steel firm awaits HK listing despite woes.

text.p: Big Chinese steelmaker Panzhihua said on Wednesday it hopes for a quick listing of its shares in Hong Kong despite a host of nagging problems in its home market.
"We hope to list H shares in Hong Kong as soon as possible," company vice president Ma Jiayuan told reporters.
Panzhihua Iron & Steel (Group) Co, one of China's biggest steelmakers, is planning to list shares of a subsidiary in the former British colony.
It already has Beijing's backing and now awaits the final go-ahead in Hong Kong, now a Special Administrative Region of China.

Ma declined to give details of the size of the share offer or say how much money would be raised, but other officials said the listed firm would be a profitable arm of the group called Panzhihua Steel and Vanadium Co Ltd.
China's steel sector is facing oversupply, sharp competition and high debts, but Ma maintained the group would be able to overcome the industry's considerable hurdles.
"The biggest problem facing enterprises such as Panzhihua is the supply of iron and steel exceeds demand," he said.
"But a product that is good can find a market."
The domestic stock market has not been kind to another recently listed steelmaker -- Bengang Steel -- which has seen its share price fall well below its offer level.
Bengang's B shares for foreign investors closed unchanged at HK$2.00 ($0.26) on the Shenzhen market on Wednesday compared with the issue price of HK$2.38.
Ma said Panzhihua's mix of products including steel plates for autos would help deflect some of the industry ailments.
Panzhihua is nestled in the rugged mountains of Sichuan province, a site chosen for its remoteness as a defence against attack in the days of China's rivalry with the former Soviet Union.
Now, Panzhihua is hoping to turn its location in southwestern China to its advantage as Beijing tries to boost development in the nation's economically backward hinterland.
"The economy of western China must be developed and 80 percent of our products are used in the western region," Ma said.
This means lower transport costs for the company, giving it a competitive advantage in this part of the country.
Panzhihua produced 3.27 million tonnes of iron and 2.82 million tonnes of steel in 1996, Ma said.
The group had total assets of 44.0 billion yuan ($5.3 billion) at the end of 1996. Last year's sales were 23.60 billion yuan and income from exports reached $266 million.
Officials made no forecast for this year's results.
The group also includes Pangang Group Steel Plate Co, a company that has A shares for domestic investors listed on south China's bourse in Shenzhen. ($1 = 8.3 yuan) ($1 = HK$7.8)
